lines.speaker: Elior
lines.text: When I was young, I thought love meant readiness. Always ready. Always enough.

lines.speaker: Elior
lines.text: After my father died, I decided the feast would not fall if I carried it. If I failed, it would mean I was not truly His.

lines.speaker: Junia
lines.text: You never told us that part.

lines.speaker: Elior
lines.text: I thought naming it would make it true. That if I admitted the fear, God would agree I had never been beloved.

lines.speaker: Keeper
lines.text: The Serpent does not invent new wounds. He teaches old ones to speak in the voice of Scripture twisted.

lines.speaker: Keeper
lines.text: But the Beloved Son was called beloved before He proved anything. Before the wilderness. Before the cross.

lines.speaker: Elior
lines.text: Abba... I have been trying to earn what was already spoken over Him — and over me.

lines.speaker: Micah
lines.text: The watch is lighter when you are not carrying alone.

lines.speaker: Elior
lines.text: I am not beloved because I grasp. I was beloved before I learned to grasp.

lines.speaker: Junia
lines.text: That is the truth the Briar could not swallow.
